issues.legal_issue: A stranger to the contract for specific performance cannot be impleaded as a defendant over the plaintiff’s objection when no relief is claimed against that stranger.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sued the vendor for specific performance of their agreement to sell; the applicant was not a party to that agreement.
While the suit was pending, and despite an injunction restraining the vendor from transferring the property, the vendor sold the property to the applicant.
The applicant sought impleadment based on the sale and a separate, alleged earlier agreement with the vendor, but the plaintiffs opposed the application and claimed no relief against the applicant.
The trial court allowed impleadment, and the High Court set that order aside.
issues.conclusion: The applicant could not be impleaded against the plaintiffs’ wish; the appeals were dismissed and the High Court’s decision was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order I Rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a necessary party must be one against whom relief is due in respect of the controversy or without whom no effective decree can be passed; a proper party must be needed to adjudicate that controversy. In a specific-performance suit, the controversy ordinarily concerns the contract between the plaintiff and the vendor. Applying Kasturi v. Iyyamperumal, (2005) 6 SCC 733, and the principle that the plaintiff is dominus litis, a stranger to that contract claiming an independent interest cannot be forced into the suit, particularly where no relief is claimed against the stranger; adding the stranger would risk enlarging the suit into a title dispute. Vijay Pratap v. Sambhu Saran Sinha, (1996) 10 SCC 53, is also relied on through Kasturi. Robin Ramjibhai Patel and Shri Swastik Developers were distinguished because there the plaintiff had sought impleadment.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and applicant_not_contract_party and plaintiff_opposes_joinder and no_relief_claimed_against_applicant

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.applicant_not_contract_party: The person seeking joinder was not a party to the agreement whose specific performance the plaintiff sought.
predicates.plaintiff_opposes_joinder: The plaintiff objected to the person’s application to be joined as a defendant.
predicates.no_relief_claimed_against_applicant: The plaintiff sought no relief against the person applying to be joined.
predicates.plaintiff_cannot_be_forced_to_join_stran: The plaintiff is not required to join the stranger as a defendant against the plaintiff’s wish.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks specific performance of a contract, the proposed defendant was not a party to it, the plaintiff opposes joinder, and no relief is sought against the proposed defendant, the plaintiff cannot be forced to join that stranger.
